authorities.name: Human Rights Act 1998, s.2(1)
authorities.date_note: Date the Act came fully into force. The text verified this session is the current in-force version.
authorities.proposition: A court or tribunal determining a question arising in connection with a Convention right must take into account any judgment, decision, declaration or advisory opinion of the European Court of Human Rights (and certain Commission/Committee of Ministers materials), whenever made, so far as the court or tribunal considers it relevant to the proceedings. The duty is to 'take into account,' not to follow automatically - the Act does not incorporate the ECHR itself, nor does it make Strasbourg case law binding.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session, on two independent passes, word-for-word consistent both times.

authorities.name: R (Ullah) v Special Adjudicator
authorities.judge_or_panel: Lord Bingham of Cornhill, Lord Steyn, Lord Walker of Gestingthorpe, Baroness Hale of Richmond, Lord Carswell
authorities.proposition: Supplies the authoritative gloss on s.2(1)'s 'take into account' duty, per Lord Bingham: 'The duty of national courts is to keep pace with the Strasbourg jurisprudence as it evolves over time: no more, but certainly no less.' This 'mirror principle' directs domestic courts to track Strasbourg case law - neither falling behind it nor, ordinarily, developing domestic rights protection beyond what Strasbourg has itself recognised. The principle was later qualified, not abandoned, in Manchester City Council v Pinnock [2010] UKSC 45 (not independently verified in this file), which held domestic courts are not bound to follow every Strasbourg decision, only a clear and constant line of authority not inconsistent with a fundamental aspect of domestic law.

The quote itself and paragraph 20 attribution within Ullah were corroborated by the researching agent via three independent secondary sources (a case-summary site, an academic notes site, and Mark Elliott's Public Law for Everyone blog), none of which this session re-fetched directly. Does not cover the Pinnock refinement in detail, the status of unincorporated UN human rights treaties in domestic law, or any other International Human Rights Law subject - all remain unbuilt.
